title: Zstandard (zstd) frame format
summary: Zstandard is a fast lossless compression algorithm developed by Facebook. A zstd frame: 4-byte magic (0x28B52FFD), frame header (window size, dictionary ID, frame content size), compressed blocks (literals + sequences), and optional checksum. Blocks are either compressed (literals Huffman + FSE sequences) or raw/RLE.

structure.meaning: Bit 7-6: Frame_Content_Size flag, bit 5: Single_Segment, bit 4: unused, bit 3-2: reserved, bit 1-0: Dictionary_ID flag.
Window size (if not single segment): exponent (5 bits) + mantissa (3 bits) -> window size = (1 << (exp+10)) + (mantissa << exp).
ID of the dictionary used (if any).
Size of the uncompressed data (if present).
Block header (3 bytes): last_block (1 bit) + block_type (2 bits: 0 compressed, 1 raw, 2 RLE, 3 reserved) + block_size (29 bits). Then block content.
Literals section (Huffman-coded) + sequences section (FSE-coded: literal lengths, offsets, match lengths).
Optional XXH64 checksum of the uncompressed data (if checksum flag set).

ext.example_decoded: zstd magic + frame header descriptor (single segment, FCS 1 byte)
notes: zstd uses Finite State Entropy (FSE) for sequence encoding and Huffman for literals.
Compression levels 1-22; higher levels use larger search windows and more thorough matching.
Dictionaries (trained on sample data) dramatically improve compression for small messages.
zstd is used by Linux kernel (module compression, btrfs, squashfs), Facebook, and many modern systems.
Skippable frames (magic 0x184D2A50) allow embedding metadata in zstd streams.
